```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(Metrics)
library(forecast)
library(pls)
```


```{r}
data  <- read.csv("../data/data_merged.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
data_mean <- read.csv("../data/prevail_mean.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
data$date <- as.Date(data$date)
data_mean$date <- as.Date(data_mean$date)
data <- data %>%
  select(date, log_ret, matches("_L[1-4]$")) %>%
  left_join(data_mean %>% select(date, mean_prevailing_ret), by = "date")

# prepare rf_df and train/test split
rf_df <- data %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  select(-mean_prevailing_ret) %>%
  drop_na()

set.seed(123)
n <- nrow(rf_df)
train_size <- floor(0.8 * n)
test_size  <- n - train_size

train_data <- rf_df[1:train_size, ]
test_data  <- rf_df[(train_size + 1):n, ]

# tuning split inside training sample (we will apply recursive CV inside training only) 
# initial training window for recursive CV (inside training)
init_train_frac <- 0.8           # fraction of training sample used as initial window
train_tune_size <- floor(init_train_frac * train_size)
val_tune_size   <- train_size - train_tune_size   # number of recursive one-step-ahead predictions to produce for validation

X_train_tune_full <- train_data %>% select(-date, -log_ret)
y_train_tune_full <- train_data$log_ret

# recursive CV on validation to choose ncomp
max_comps <- min(20, ncol(X_train_tune_full))
if (max_comps < 1) stop("No predictors found for PCR tuning.")

val_rmse_vec <- numeric(max_comps)

for (ncomp in 1:max_comps) {
  # produce recursive (expanding-window) one-step-ahead preds across validation portion
  val_preds_recursive <- numeric(val_tune_size)
  for (i in 1:val_tune_size) {
    # expanding window: use observations 1 : (train_tune_size + i - 1) to predict next point (train_tune_size + i)
    train_idx_end <- train_tune_size + i - 1
    train_subset <- train_data[1:train_idx_end, ]
    val_point    <- train_data[train_idx_end + 1, , drop = FALSE]
    
    X_train_sub <- train_subset %>% select(-date, -log_ret)
    y_train_sub <- train_subset$log_ret
    X_val_point <- val_point %>% select(-date, -log_ret)
    
    pcr_sub <- pcr(
      y_train_sub ~ .,
      data = cbind(y_train_sub, X_train_sub),
      ncomp = ncomp,
      scale = TRUE,
      center = TRUE,
      validation = "none"
    )
    pred_val <- as.numeric(predict(pcr_sub, newdata = X_val_point, ncomp = ncomp))
    val_preds_recursive[i] <- pred_val
  }
  # true validation targets (the val_tune_size points)
  y_val_true <- train_data$log_ret[(train_tune_size + 1):train_size]
  val_rmse_vec[ncomp] <- sqrt(mean((y_val_true - val_preds_recursive)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
}



best_ncomp <- which.min(val_rmse_vec)
best_val_rmse <- val_rmse_vec[best_ncomp]

# Plot: Validation RMSE vs ncomp
val_df <- data.frame(ncomp = 1:max_comps, val_rmse = val_rmse_vec)
p_valcurve <- ggplot(val_df, aes(x = ncomp, y = val_rmse)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = best_ncomp, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = best_ncomp, y = min(val_rmse_vec), label = paste0("best n=", best_ncomp),
           vjust = -1, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Validation RMSE vs PCR components (recursive CV on training)", x = "Number of components", y = "Validation RMSE") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p_valcurve)

# Fit final PCR model once on full training set using best_ncomp
X_train_full <- train_data %>% select(-date, -log_ret)
y_train_full <- train_data$log_ret

pcr_final <- pcr(
  y_train_full ~ .,
  data = cbind(y_train_full, X_train_full),
  ncomp = best_ncomp,
  scale = TRUE,
  center = TRUE,
  validation = "none"
)

# Predict on test set
X_test_full <- test_data %>% select(-date, -log_ret)
pcr_test_preds <- as.numeric(predict(pcr_final, newdata = X_test_full, ncomp = best_ncomp))

# attach predictions to rf_df aligned with test indices
rf_df$pcr_forecast_ret <- c(rep(NA, train_size), pcr_test_preds)

# Prepare plotting dataframe (include prevailing mean)
plot_pcr_df <- rf_df %>%
  left_join(data %>% select(date, mean_prevailing_ret), by = "date")
```


```{r}
# Plot: Actual vs Prevailing mean vs PCR (TEST SET)
plot_test <- plot_pcr_df %>% tail(test_size)
p_ts <- ggplot(plot_test, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = log_ret, color = "Actual")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_prevailing_ret, color = "Prevailing mean")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pcr_forecast_ret, color = "PCR"), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual" = "black", "Prevailing mean" = "blue", "PCR" = "darkgreen")) +
  labs(title = "Test set: Actual vs Prevailing Mean vs PCR (final model predicts test set)", x = "Date", y = "Log Return", color = "") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p_ts)

# Scatter: Actual vs Predicted (PCR)
scatter_df <- plot_test %>% filter(!is.na(pcr_forecast_ret))
p_scatter <- ggplot(scatter_df, aes(x = pcr_forecast_ret, y = log_ret)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Actual vs PCR Predicted (TEST)", x = "PCR predicted", y = "Actual") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p_scatter)

# Residuals time plot
resid_df <- scatter_df %>% mutate(resid_pcr = log_ret - pcr_forecast_ret)
p_resid <- ggplot(resid_df, aes(x = date, y = resid_pcr)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "PCR Residuals (Test set)", x = "Date", y = "Residual (Actual - Pred)") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p_resid)
```


```{r}
# Compute metrics
actual_pcr <- test_data$log_ret
pred_pcr   <- pcr_test_preds

MAE_pcr  <- mean(abs(actual_pcr - pred_pcr), na.rm = TRUE)
RMSE_pcr <- sqrt(mean((actual_pcr - pred_pcr)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
R2_pcr   <- cor(actual_pcr, pred_pcr, use = "complete.obs")^2

metrics_tbl <- data.frame(
  Model = "PCR",
  MAE = MAE_pcr,
  RMSE = RMSE_pcr,
  R2 = R2_pcr,
  ncomp = best_ncomp,
  val_RMSE = best_val_rmse
)
print(metrics_tbl)
```


```{r}
# DM Test (simple): use test set errors
pcr_eval_df <- plot_test %>%
  filter(!is.na(pcr_forecast_ret) & !is.na(mean_prevailing_ret)) %>%
  mutate(
    err_pcr  = log_ret - pcr_forecast_ret,
    err_mean = log_ret - mean_prevailing_ret
  )

if (nrow(pcr_eval_df) < 2) {
  message("Not enough observations with both forecasts to run DM test (need >= 2).")
} else {
  dm_test_pcr <- dm.test(e1 = pcr_eval_df$err_pcr, e2 = pcr_eval_df$err_mean, alternative = "less")
  print(dm_test_pcr)
  if (dm_test_pcr$p.value < 0.05) {
    cat("Conclusion: PCR significantly outperforms the Prevailing Mean model (lower forecast error).\n")
  } else {
    cat("Conclusion: PCR does NOT significantly outperform the Prevailing Mean model.\n")
  }
}


```
